paraphrase: Gorakṣa displays a body made adamantine (vajrakāya) that no sword can cut; the sword passes through Allama's body without meeting anything, and Gorakṣa recognizes the void body as higher than the imperishable one.
speaker: Cāmarasa (narrator)
notes: Skeleton from memory; locator is the incipit (or a descriptive key when the incipit is not recalled) because vacana numbering differs between editions — fix against the Samagra Vacana Sāhitya in Phase D. Gorakṣa's claim is presented by a Vīraśaiva poet. Canto numbers not recalled.

paraphrase: Māyā, drawn to Allama as he plays the drum in the temple, pursues him; he remains untouched, and her desire cannot bind one who has no second.

paraphrase: Allama is Śiva's own descent into the world; Pārvatī, doubting his detachment, sends her tāmasic aspect as Māyā, born as a princess of Banavāsi, to win him.
